title: "Gender Inequality Change, 2010–2019"
author: "LingziZhuo"
output: html_document
---

## Research question

How did gender inequality change across countries between 2010 and 2019?

## Measure of change

We calculate change as:

GII change = GII in 2019 - GII in 2010

- A negative value indicates a decrease in gender inequality.
- A positive value indicates an increase in gender inequality.
- Zero indicates no change in the reported index.

## Check the project folder

```{r check-folder}
getwd()
```
## Read the original data

```{r read-data}
gii_raw <- read.csv(
  "../data/HDR25_Composite_indices_complete_time_series.csv"
)

dim(gii_raw)
head(names(gii_raw), 20)
```
## Locate the GII columns

```{r inspect-gii}
required_columns <- c("iso3", "country", "gii_2010", "gii_2019")

required_columns %in% names(gii_raw)

str(gii_raw[required_columns])

head(gii_raw[required_columns])
```
## Calculate GII change

```{r calculate-change}
gii <- gii_raw[required_columns]

gii$gii_change <- gii$gii_2019 - gii$gii_2010

head(gii)

colSums(is.na(gii[c("gii_2010", "gii_2019", "gii_change")]))
```
## Check country identifiers

```{r check-identifiers}
anyDuplicated(gii$iso3)

tail(gii, 12)
```
## Separate country records from aggregates

```{r filter-countries}
is_country <- grepl("^[A-Z]{3}$", gii$iso3)

gii[!is_country, c("iso3", "country")]

gii_countries <- gii[is_country, ]

nrow(gii_countries)
sum(!is.na(gii_countries$gii_change))
```
After excluding 11 aggregate records, the dataset contains 195
country or territory records. Of these, 154 have GII values for
both 2010 and 2019, allowing the change to be calculated.
The remaining 41 records have missing change values.
## Prepare spatial analysis

```{r load-sf}
library(sf)
```
## Read the world boundaries

```{r read-world}
world <- st_read(
  "../data/World_Countries_(Generalized)_2173680399808997149.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
)

nrow(world)
names(world)
head(st_drop_geometry(world))
```
## Standardise country codes

```{r standardise-codes}
library(countrycode)

world$iso3 <- countrycode(
  world$ISO,
  origin = "iso2c",
  destination = "iso3c"
)

head(st_drop_geometry(world)[c("COUNTRY", "ISO", "iso3")])

st_drop_geometry(world)[is.na(world$iso3), c("COUNTRY", "ISO")]
```
## Join GII data to world boundaries

```{r join-data}
match_row <- match(world$iso3, gii_countries$iso3)

world_gii <- world

world_gii$gii_2010 <- gii_countries$gii_2010[match_row]
world_gii$gii_2019 <- gii_countries$gii_2019[match_row]
world_gii$gii_change <- gii_countries$gii_change[match_row]

nrow(world_gii)
sum(!is.na(match_row))
sum(!is.na(world_gii$gii_change))

head(st_drop_geometry(world_gii)[
  c("COUNTRY", "iso3", "gii_2010", "gii_2019", "gii_change")
])
```
## Check repeated map codes

```{r check-map-duplicates}
repeated_code <- duplicated(world$iso3) |
  duplicated(world$iso3, fromLast = TRUE)

st_drop_geometry(world)[
  repeated_code,
  c("COUNTRY", "ISO", "iso3")
]
```
## Check coverage by unique country code

```{r check-coverage}
length(unique(world_gii$iso3[!is.na(match_row)]))

length(unique(
  world_gii$iso3[!is.na(world_gii$gii_change)]
))

gii_countries[
  !gii_countries$iso3 %in% world$iso3,
  c("country", "iso3", "gii_change")
]
```
```{r map-gii, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
breaks <- c(-1, -0.10, -0.05, 0, 0.05, 0.10, 1)

palette <- c(
  "#2166AC", "#67A9CF", "#D1E5F0",
  "#FDDBC7", "#EF8A62", "#B2182B"
)

change_group <- cut(
  world_gii$gii_change,
  breaks = breaks,
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

map_colours <- palette[as.integer(change_group)]
map_colours[is.na(world_gii$gii_change)] <- "grey85"

plot(
  st_geometry(world_gii),
  col = map_colours,
  border = "grey50",
  main = "GII change: 2019 minus 2010"
)

legend(
  "bottomleft",
  legend = c(
    "[-1, -0.10]", "(-0.10, -0.05]", "(-0.05, 0]",
    "(0, 0.05]", "(0.05, 0.10]", "(0.10, 1]",
    "No data"
  ),
  fill = c(palette, "grey85"),
  title = "Change in GII",
  cex = 0.7,
  bg = "white"
)
```
## Summarise the direction of change

```{r summarise-change}
change <- gii_countries$gii_change

c(
  decreased = sum(change < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  unchanged = sum(change == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  increased = sum(change > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  missing = sum(is.na(change))
)
```
## Findings and limitations

Among the 154 countries or territories with GII data for both
2010 and 2019, 145 (94.2%) recorded a decrease in GII and
9 (5.8%) recorded an increase. None had an exactly zero change
in the reported values.

A further 41 records lacked sufficient data to calculate change.
The findings therefore describe countries and territories with
available data, rather than every country or territory.

The map shows changes in GII, not the level of GII in 2019.
A large decrease does not necessarily mean that the final level
of gender inequality was low. This descriptive comparison does
not establish the causes of change.

## Data sources and method

GII data were obtained from the UNDP Human Development Report
2025 composite indices time-series dataset. Values for 2010
and 2019 were taken from the same release.

Source: <https://hdr.undp.org/data-center/documentation-and-downloads>

World boundaries were obtained from the World Countries
Generalized dataset in GeoJSON format.

Source: <https://hub.arcgis.com/datasets/2b93b06dc0dc4e809d3c8db5cb96ba69_0/explore>

Eleven aggregate records were excluded from the GII table.
Two-letter boundary codes were converted to three-letter ISO
codes using the countrycode package. The datasets were then
matched by these codes.

Change was calculated as GII in 2019 minus GII in 2010.
Missing values were retained. Summary counts used the GII
country table to avoid counting separate map parts more than once.

## Reproducing the analysis

Open the RStudio project. The required packages are rmarkdown,
sf and countrycode.

Place the original UNDP CSV and world boundaries GeoJSON in
the data folder, retaining the filenames used in this document.
Open practical4_homework/homework_gii.Rmd and click Knit.
